title: [Installer] Preserve MSI file ownership with Smart Cabbing

proposed_comments.title: Publish preview handlers for the local installer script

confidence.rationale: The local build script supplies CIBuild=true without publishing preview handlers. Executing the changed event with those flags reaches harvesting without publishing.

proposed_comments.body:
### Publish preview handlers for the local installer script

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** The new `CIBuild` guard in the native pre-build event and `tools/build/build-installer.ps1`'s local installer workflow.

**Problem:** The local script passes `/p:CIBuild=true /p:IsPipeline=true`, but does not publish the four preview handlers before building the installer. This new guard consequently skips `publish.cmd` for that local path too. The script's MSBuild `IsPipeline` property is not the environment variable tested by the former WiX event.

**Why it matters:** Harvesting can consume ordinary build outputs instead of the published preview-handler payload; the installer documentation explicitly requires publishing for correct WebView2 DLL inclusion.

**Suggested change:** Distinguish genuinely prepublished pipeline inputs from the local script's build flags. Ensure the local workflow publishes the preview handlers before harvesting, while preserving the no-republish path for real CI inputs. Cover the actual local-script flags in the event-ordering regression rather than assuming every `CIBuild=true` invocation has published already.

**Verification:** A command fixture executing the exact event with `CIBuild=true` and no `IsPipeline` environment variable reached harvesting without calling publish. The local script has no separate preview-handler publish step. This proves the skipped step; a complete MSI payload build was not run.

proposed_comments.title: Normalize the platform passed to the publish profiles

confidence.rationale: The solution uses ARM64, the publish profile overrides the common lowercase RID with win-$(Platform), and the self-contained SDK check rejects win-ARM64 but accepts win-arm64.

proposed_comments.body:
### Normalize the platform passed to the publish profiles

**Severity:** `medium`

The installer solution uses `ARM64`, but `publish.cmd` forwards this argument into profiles that set `RuntimeIdentifier` to `win-$(Platform)`. Those profiles overwrite the earlier lowercase value from `Common.SelfContained.props`, so a local ARM64 publish can fail with `NETSDK1083` for `win-ARM64`. Preserve the previous WiX event's lowercase publish argument:

```suggestion
      call "$(ProjectDir)..\PowerToysSetupVNext\publish.cmd" $(Platform.ToLowerInvariant())
```

The literal replacement parses as XML and evaluates to `arm64` under MSBuild. An isolated self-contained SDK framework-reference check rejects `win-ARM64` and passes with `win-arm64`; this is not a full ARM64 installer build.

proposed_comments.title: Restore the harvested templates if the media pass fails

confidence.rationale: The new final media pass throws on missing source files after templates are mutated. Reproducing that failure and retrying the exact harvester corrupts the file-list define.

proposed_comments.body:
### Restore the harvested templates if the media pass fails

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** The final `Set-InstallerMedia` call, the native pre-build template backups, and the WiX post-build restoration.

**Problem:** The new media pass hashes sources after harvesting has mutated the WXS templates. If a source disappears or cannot be read, that pass throws before the parent WiX build reaches restoration. Retrying then overwrites the original backups with generated authoring; `Generate-FileList` replaces only the define prefix and appends the previous list to the new one.

**Why it matters:** A transient media-generation failure can make subsequent installer builds fail on nonexistent filenames even after the original source problem is repaired.

**Suggested change:** Restore all mutated WXS/header templates when harvesting or media generation fails, before a retry can overwrite their original backups. Keep the failure visible to MSBuild. Also make file-list replacement retry-safe, and add a failure-then-retry regression that exercises this cleanup boundary, not just two successful harvest/restore cycles.

**Verification:** After the exact harvester generated one `PowerDisplay.ico` entry, removing its source made `Set-InstallerMedia` throw. Repeating the pre-build backup and harvest after restoring the source produced `PowerDisplay.icoPowerDisplay.ico` in the define. The new bounded media markers and PowerDisplay backup fix successful cycles, but neither restores templates on this failure path.
